Team —

Thanks again for taking the time to interview Riley yesterday. I'm trying to close the loop on feedback so we can either move to an offer or close the loop by EOW. Two asks:

1) Please upload your completed scorecard to the shared folder and attach any notes (I've attached my draft scorecards as riley_scorecards.pdf and logan_notes_riley.docx).
2) Call out any hard red flags or conflicting signals in a short line in reply — I want the consensus to be explicit (pass / hold / decline + short rationale).

Quick calibration notes:
- We're weighing system design and on-the-job debugging higher than algorithms for this role. Candidates with clear communication under ambiguous constraints get a +1.
- On the rubric, treat "ownership examples" as tie-breaker when technical scores are within 1 point.

If we can't reach consensus asynchronously by Tuesday 12/22 12:00 PST I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Tuesday afternoon. Simon (external recruiter) is on the loop to align timelines — copying him for visibility.

Attachments: riley_scorecards.pdf, logan_notes_riley.docx

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Recruiting Coordinator | Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — uploaded my scorecard (marissa_scorecard_riley.pdf) and left inline comments in the doc. Quick summary from my side:
- Technical: 7/10 (solid API design, missed an optimization for KV cache handling)
- System design: 8/10 (good trade-offs, thought about operational constraints)
- Communication: 6/10 (concise but a few gaps when probed on latency SLOs)
- Ownership: 8/10 (clear examples)

Recommendation: proceed to take-home assignment (I'd like to see a short implementation to validate latency/scale reasoning) — not a blocker for an offer but would reduce risk.

Marissa
Sr. SWE, Infra

Appreciate the summary. My quick take:
- Overall score: 6.5/10 averaged across sections.
- Red flags: limited experience with quantization and kernel selection for our stack — candidate gave high-level answers but lacked concrete examples.
- Positive: excellent debugging framework and culture fit in hypothetical on-call scenarios.

Recommendation: hold for a focused systems deep-dive (20–30 min) rather than a full take-home. If they can clearly articulate a kernel selection/quantization plan, we can move forward.

Irene
Staff SWE

Thanks all — summary and next steps:

Panel scores averaged ~6.9/10. There are consistent concerns around quantization+kernel depth and slightly mixed communication signals. Consensus path:
- Schedule a 25-min focused deep-dive with Irene + Soojin to cover kernel selection & quantization examples.
- Marissa: please hold off the take-home for now; we will make a call after the deep-dive.
- Simon: please tentatively hold the offer window; if deep-dive is successful we will aim to extend within 72 hours.

Action items:
- Logan: schedule the deep-dive (I put a tentative 12/23 9:30am PST on the calendar — will update to confirm availability)
- Irene & Soojin: prepare 3 targeted prompts/whiteboard questions
- Marissa: update scorecard with final note after deep-dive
- Simon: keep candidate informed on timeline (no offer yet)

Attachments: riley_scorecards.pdf, logan_notes_riley.docx, marissa_scorecard_riley.pdf
